answer: Because the spiral index resolves every citation against the horizon checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the cedar audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 257 aliases as a result forfeits the authoring cost 257 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. A farm of 2427 identities would post 3671 proofs and burn roughly 33 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is a coat check that never returns the coat: the room looks crowded, but every person inside already paid to be there.
